retiredPacks.retiredBecause: Fails spec §5.10. The independent round of 4 September 2026 judged 3 of its 7 questions answerable with no pack at all, and the remaining questions substitute the pack’s numerals into q = F / (p - v), a relationship the candidate already holds. Every block is textbook cost-volume-profit: the assumption list, the formula and the no-break-even case are all standard. There is no non-generic element in the subject to retarget the failing questions onto, and adding one would be replacement dressed as repair. Kept as the evidence for §5.10; counts for nothing. A replacement should keep the text-plus-assumptions-plus-formula-plus-figure shape and the business-administration or economics domain, and be built on a scheme the source defines itself — a stated costing or allocation rule with its own conventions — rather than on a formula the candidate can be assumed to know.

packs.title: A supplier’s step rebate scheme

raisedIssues: gam-ba-sr-001-q2: an independent adjudicator found it settled by gam-ba-sr-001-q1, gam-ba-sr-001-q3, gam-ba-sr-001-q4, gam-ba-sr-001-q5 (spec §5.9)
gam-ba-sr-001-q3: an independent adjudicator found it settled by gam-ba-sr-001-q1, gam-ba-sr-001-q2, gam-ba-sr-001-q4, gam-ba-sr-001-q5 (spec §5.9)

contributesUnderSection510.whatItContributes: An entirely invented, non-standard rebate mechanism — the band thresholds and rates, the formula applying the band's rate to the whole year's quantity rather than marginally, the list-price-only basis, and the retrospective withdraw-and-resettle-on-return rule — none of which is generic business knowledge a candidate could supply unaided.

blockers: 2 question(s) an adjudicator could narrow using a sibling: gam-ba-sr-001-q4, gam-ba-sr-001-q5
not signed off by a person

decisions.question: An adjudicator shown these questions with no source at all judged 2 of them settled by a sibling: gam-ba-sr-001-q2, gam-ba-sr-001-q3. Is that judgement right, and if it is, does the pack need rebuilding?

evidence.detail: Every sibling treats 'the rebate' as one lump value attached to a buyer's annual unit total, never as a sum of per-band marginal slices: q1 asks for a single 'rebate due' on a total; q3 talks about withdrawing and re-settling a single rebate per buyer; q4 asks what a single rebate is 'worked out on'; q5's option (d) frames clearing a threshold as unlocking one rebate on that year's total. That consistent all-units framing across four independent items is exactly the fact q2 turns on, and it points at option (c).

Laying every unit figure in the pack side by side (620, 880, 900, 950, 1,520, 1,700, 1,800) shows a consistent multiple-of-300 pattern: q2's boundary sits right at 900, q5's 1,800 is a clean multiple of 300, q1's 950 sits just above 900, and q4's 620 sits just above 600 — all consistent with band edges at 300/600/900/1,200/1,500/1,800. Under that reconstructed spacing, buyer 1's 1,520 (just above the 1,500 edge) drops to 1,480 (below it) after returning 40 units, while buyer 2's 1,700 drops only to 1,660, staying inside the same 1,500-1,799 band. That arithmetic, built entirely from sibling numbers, directly resolves the mechanic q3 asks about and points decisively at option (c).

decisions.ifAccepted: The pack clears its last automated blocker and needs only sign-off.
decisions.ifNotAccepted: The coupled questions must be rebuilt, which retires this round and requires a fresh one.

decisions.question: 2 question(s) can be narrowed — not settled — using a sibling: gam-ba-sr-001-q4, gam-ba-sr-001-q5. Is the cost to each item acceptable, or must they be rebuilt? Spec §5.9 leaves this to a person because severity is a judgement.

evidence.detail: q1 ('purchases ... come to 950 units') and q3 ('credited with a rebate ... on a year's total of 1,520 units') both establish that band membership in this scheme is counted in physical units, not purchase value. That decisively rules out option (c) ('does not count towards the band'), since a price cut on one order doesn't change how many units were bought. It doesn't settle the a/b/d contest over what the rebate is computed on.

q2 and q3 together establish (see their own leakDetail entries) that this is an all-units/retroactive scheme with fixed calendar-year bands roughly 300 units wide. Under a retroactive scheme, concentrating volume in one year yields a strictly bigger blended rate than splitting, which reinforces (rather than creates) the standalone lean toward option (a).

evidence.detail: If SPLIT scales linearly with catalogue size n, then SPLIT(256) ≈ (this answer) × 256/1024, which would allow a test-taker to compute the SCAN(256) residual in q5 by subtraction. Similarly, SPLIT(4096) ≈ (this answer) × 4, and q7 requires 4096 × SPLIT(4096), creating an arithmetic link.

If a test-taker determines that SPLIT > SCAN at exactly one size (or at none, or at multiple), this directly constrains q6's answer about what holds across all sizes. For example, if q3's answer is 'at n = 4096 only', then q6 cannot claim a rule holds at every size.

If SPLIT scales linearly, q2's answer constrains SPLIT(256) = (q2 answer) × 256/1024. Subtracting this from the total (q5 options) would reveal SCAN(256), and the options become narrower. For instance, if q2 = 315 (option c), then SPLIT(256) ≈ 79, meaning SCAN(256) ≈ option - 79. This creates a strong narrowing leak.

If q3 determines that SPLIT > SCAN at exactly one size, this rules out q6 option d ('at none of the three sizes'). Conversely, if q3 says SPLIT > SCAN at multiple sizes, this affects which routing statement in q6 is universally true.

If SPLIT scales predictably (e.g., linearly) with catalogue size, q2's answer for SPLIT(1024) allows estimation of SPLIT(4096) ≈ (q2 answer) × 4. Then total ≈ 4096 × (q2 answer × 4) ≈ 16384 × (q2 answer). For q2 option c (315), this gives ~5.2M, close to q7 option c. This arithmetic link is a narrowing leak.

contributesUnderSection510.whatItContributes: The specific adequacy guidance (p4: U-value must not exceed 0.28 W/m2K) that this text stipulates for judging a wall's compliance - a threshold and choice of quantity (U rather than Q or R) that cannot be derived from thermal physics alone.

not signed off by a person

decisions.question: An adjudicator shown these questions with no source at all judged 3 of them settled by a sibling: gam-eng-tr-001-q3, gam-eng-tr-001-q4, gam-eng-tr-001-q6. Is that judgement right, and if it is, does the pack need rebuilding?

evidence.detail: If q3 answer is B (insulation dominates), then q4's question 'By what factor does heat flow change if brick thickness doubles?' becomes nearly deterministic: Q' / Q = R_total / (2×R_brick + R_insulation) ≈ R_total / R_total ≈ 1 (option a, unchanged). Similarly, q6 asks which change reduces U-value to compliance; if insulation dominates, adding more insulation (option c) is the only effective answer.

q3 establishes that insulation contributes much more resistance than brick. If this answer is accepted, then q4 becomes nearly solved: doubling brick barely changes the total when insulation dominates. The answer is option a, making this a decisive leak from q3.

q3 establishes that insulation controls thermal resistance. Therefore, the change that most effectively reduces U-value (increases R) is adding insulation. q3's answer makes q6 option c nearly forced. This is a decisive leak.

contributesUnderSection510.whatItContributes: A specific three-part source-evaluation framework (attribution/proximity/interest checks) with precise scope boundaries (e.g. proximity excludes honesty; interest excludes distance; corroboration requires independence, not copy count; a failed check only disqualifies evidence for questions that check governs) that must be applied exactly as defined to classify each scenario correctly.

evidence.detail: q2 establishes a key principle: failing a source check does not disqualify a document for all purposes. This principle is central to q4, which asks whether a document with wrong attribution is usable for a question that does not turn on who wrote it. The principle demonstrated in q2 directly informs q4's reasoning.
